newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels begin moving Rwandan refugees by night.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels begin moving Rwandan refugees by night.

text.p: Zairean rebel authorities have started moving huge numbers of refugees to Kisangani by night, swiftly threatening to overwhelm United Nations aid facilities set up to airlift them home, aid officials said on Wednesday.
Aid officials said a second train full of refugees arrived unexpectedly in Kisangani on Wednesday night and they were scrambling to accommodate them at a transit camp near the international airport.
"The (rebel) Alliance seems to have adopted the repatriation with a new round of zealousness," said Paul Stromberg, spokesman for the United Nations refugee agency, UNHCR.

After weeks of delaying a planned airlift of an estimated 100,000 refugees scattered in dense jungle south of Kisangani, the Zairean rebels said on Sunday the U.N. had 60 days to repatriate all those remaining.
"Between no repatriation and what is happening now is a big gulf," said Stromberg. "If we do not recieve the cooperation of the Alliance we cannot cope."
Over 200 refugees left Kisangani by air for Rwanda's capital Kigali on Wednesday, the first since the rebels gave the go-ahead on Sunday for the repatriation to begin.
